subject: ai
question: Differentiate between A* and AO* algorithms.
title: A-star Path, AO-star Plan
hook: One walks a path. One builds a plan.
answer: Graph: A* works on an OR graph; AO* works on an AND-OR graph
Solution: A* gives a single path from start to goal; AO* gives a solution graph (sub-problem tree containing every branch of each AND)
Cost: A* ranks nodes by f(n) = g(n) + h(n); in AO* the cost of an AND arc is the sum of its children's costs
Update: A* has no back-propagation of costs; AO* revises costs backwards up to the parents after expanding a node
Use: A* for pathfinding; AO* for problem decomposition. Both are optimal if h never over-estimates
